---
title: "Data quality evaluation"
params:
  norm_method: "loess_norm"
  interactive_plot: false        # Not used here; passed by the app to both reports
  project_title: ""
  generated_at: ""               # Time of generation, set by the app (also in the file name)
  on_serve: false                # Generated on SciLifeLab Serve (hosting acknowledgement)
format:
  html:
    theme: cosmo
    toc: true
    toc-location: left
    toc-depth: 3
    toc-title: "Contents"
    number-sections: false       # Numbers in the headings: the same as in the app (see below)
    embed-resources: true
    page-layout: full
    fig-width: 10
    fig-height: 5
    mainfont: "Lato, 'Segoe UI', sans-serif"
execute:
  echo: false
  warning: false
  message: false
  output: true                   # Overrides `output: asis` of _quarto.yml (widgets, tables)
---

<!--
  Internal report of QuaNTA. Rendered by the app in a background process, in a private copy of
  this folder (scripts/render_report.R); the data are the session's own files, found through the
  session parameter file (QUANTA_PARAMS_FILE). Parts are in chapters/internal-*.qmd:
  - internal-status.qmd and internal-calibration.qmd: only with calibration (targeted mode)
  - internal-norm-method.qmd: one section per normalization method (`NORM_M`)
  The layout follows the quality control reports of MeTaQuaC (see References).
  Section numbers are written in the headings: chapters 2-4 follow the pages of the app, and a
  table or figure that is also in the app has the app's number (e.g. 3.8); sections only in this
  report are numbered under the related one (e.g. 3.8.1) or in chapters 1 and 5.
-->

```{r}
chapters_dir <- file.path(app_root, "reports", "chapters")
```

```{=html}
<script>
  // All plotly plots (widgets and viewers): a light grey plot area, as in the app
  (function patch() {
    if (!window.Plotly) return setTimeout(patch, 100);
    if (Plotly.__quantaBg) return;
    Plotly.__quantaBg = true;
    ["newPlot", "react"].forEach(function (fn) {
      var orig = Plotly[fn];
      Plotly[fn] = function (gd, data, layout) {
        var lay = (data && !Array.isArray(data) && data.layout) ? data.layout : layout;
        if (lay && typeof lay === "object") {
          lay.plot_bgcolor = "#F4F5F7";
          // Large numbers on the axes in scientific notation (1E+4), not as 10k (as in the app)
          Object.keys(lay).forEach(function (k) {
            var ax = lay[k];
            if (/^[xy]axis[0-9]*$/.test(k) && ax && typeof ax === "object" && !ax.exponentformat) ax.exponentformat = "E";
          });
        }
        return orig.apply(this, arguments);
      };
    });
  })();
  // Plots drawn before the hook (if any) are recoloured
  setInterval(function () {
    if (!window.Plotly) return;
    document.querySelectorAll(".js-plotly-plot").forEach(function (el) {
      if (!el._fullLayout) return;
      var upd = {};
      if (el._fullLayout.plot_bgcolor !== "#F4F5F7") upd.plot_bgcolor = "#F4F5F7";
      // Scientific axis labels also for these plots (unless a plot sets its own format)
      Object.keys(el._fullLayout).forEach(function (k) {
        if (!/^[xy]axis[0-9]*$/.test(k)) return;
        var own = el.layout && el.layout[k] && el.layout[k].exponentformat;
        var fa = el._fullLayout[k];
        if (!own && fa.exponentformat !== "E") upd[k + ".exponentformat"] = "E";
        // Plotly writes exponents from 10000 on: from 1000 on as e.g. 2.5e+3 (as in the app)
        if (fa.type !== "linear" || !fa.range) return;
        el.__qTf = el.__qTf || {};
        var own_tf = el.layout && el.layout[k] && el.layout[k].tickformat && !el.__qTf[k];
        var m = Math.max(Math.abs(+fa.range[0]), Math.abs(+fa.range[1]));
        var want = m >= 1000 && m < 10000;
        if (!own_tf && want && !el.__qTf[k]) { upd[k + ".tickformat"] = ".2~e"; el.__qTf[k] = true; }
        if (!want && el.__qTf[k]) { upd[k + ".tickformat"] = ""; el.__qTf[k] = false; }
      });
      if (Object.keys(upd).length) Plotly.relayout(el, upd);
    });
  }, 1000);
  // Plots in tabs that were hidden at load time get their full width when the tab is opened
  document.addEventListener('shown.bs.tab', () => window.dispatchEvent(new Event('resize')));
  // The logos into the title block (built by Quarto)
  document.addEventListener('DOMContentLoaded', function () {
    var logos = document.querySelector('.report-logos'), header = document.getElementById('title-block-header');
    if (logos && header) header.insertBefore(logos, header.firstChild);
  });
</script>
```

```{r}
#| label: setup
options(box.path = Sys.getenv("R_BOX_PATH", "app/"))
box::use(SumExp, util = projlib/msdial_utils, proc = projlib/proc, show = projlib/show,
         msdial = projlib/msdial, ggplot2[...])
library(dplyr, warn.conflicts = FALSE)
# Light grey plot area with grey grid lines (as the interactive plots, see the styles above)
theme_set(theme_minimal(base_size = 14) +
            theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
                  panel.background = element_rect(fill = "#F4F5F7", colour = NA),
                  panel.grid.major = element_line(colour = "#C8CDD5")))

# The session's data (paths from the session parameter file)
user_inputs <- msdial$get_user_input()
raw <- msdial$read_parsed_msdial_data(user_inputs)
tr <- readRDS(msdial$get_raw_data_file_name(user_inputs, suffix = "to_report"))
stopifnot("Processing NOT completed." = isTRUE(tr[["Completed"]]))
MAT <- params$norm_method
BLK <- util$mat_id_of_blank_subtracted(MAT)
# Time of generation (also in the file name when generated by the app)
GENERATED_AT <- if (nzchar(params$generated_at)) params$generated_at else format(Sys.time(), "%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S %Z")
# Calibration (targeted mode only); batches without any calibration are left out
proc_file <- msdial$get_raw_data_file_name(user_inputs, suffix = "proc")
lst <- if (!isTRUE(SumExp::metadata(raw)$is_non_target_mode) && file.exists(proc_file)) {
  Filter(\(x) !is.null(x$concn), readRDS(proc_file)[[BLK]])
}
HAS_CALIB <- length(lst) > 0
unit <- user_inputs$concentration_unit
method_label <- c(raw = "Raw", loess_norm = "LOESS", closest_norm = "Closest RT", mvis_norm = "Multivariate (PCA)")
method_label <- method_label[names(method_label) %in% names(tr[["normalized"]])]
norm_desc <- c(
  closest_norm = "Each feature is divided by the internal standard closest in retention time.",
  loess_norm = paste("Each sample is normalized by a LOESS fit [@cleveland1988] of the internal standards",
                     "over the retention time, so that signal changes that depend on the retention time are corrected."),
  mvis_norm = paste("The variation shared by all internal standards (their first principal component) is",
                    "removed from every feature [@surowiec2017].")
)
# Batch IDs of the data; "all" in one-batch mode
batch_label <- function(b) ifelse(b == "all", "All samples", paste("Batch", b))

# Features
feat <- SumExp::row_df(raw) |>
  tibble::as_tibble(rownames = "feature_id") |>
  mutate(type = case_when(
    .std_type == "vIS" ~ "Volumetric IS",
    util$is_internal_std(.std_type) ~ "Internal standard",
    util$is_targeted_feature(.std_type) ~ "Targeted",
    TRUE ~ "Non-targeted"
  ),
  # Unknown (non-targeted) features are named by their m/z and retention time
  label = ifelse(type == "Non-targeted", sprintf("Unk_%.4f_%.2f", mz, .rt), feature_name))

# Samples; `group` = study class, or the control category
smp <- SumExp::col_df(raw) |>
  tibble::as_tibble(rownames = "sample_id") |>
  mutate(category = ifelse(.ctrl_cat == "", "Study sample", .ctrl_cat),
         group = show$sample_group(SumExp::col_df(raw)))
study_classes <- sort(unique(smp$Class[smp$category == "Study sample"]))
# Colours shared with the app (projlib/show.R)
group_colors <- show$sample_group_colors(smp$group)
class_colors <- group_colors[study_classes]
# Colour-blind safe (Okabe-Ito), as the sample groups
cat_colors <- c("Study sample" = "#009E73", "QC" = "#0072B2", "Blank" = "#D55E00", "CalCurve" = "#999999")
batch_ids <- if (HAS_CALIB) names(lst) else unique(as.character(smp$batch_id))

# QC samples are only shown when the data has them
has_qc <- any(smp$category == "QC")
has_qc_rep <- proc$has_qc_replicates(raw)
NO_QC <- "No QC samples in this dataset."
note <- function(txt) knitr::asis_output(paste0('<p class="note-line">', txt, '</p>'))

# Concentrations of all batches (long format) with a status per compound and sample
conc_long <- purrr::map_dfr(lst, function(x) {
  d <- SumExp::as_tibble(x$concn) |>
    select(.row_id, feature_name, sample_name, Class, .ctrl_cat, injection_order, batch_id,
           conc, conc0, lod, lloq, max_c_conc, any_of("uloq"), has_proper_range, src_calcurve, any_of("conc_flag"))
  if (!"conc_flag" %in% names(d)) d$conc_flag <- NA_character_   # Processed by older versions
  if (!"uloq" %in% names(d)) d$uloq <- d$max_c_conc   # Older versions: the top level of every curve
  mutate(d, conc_flag = as.character(conc_flag))
})
# Values below the LOD / LLOQ: replaced (LLOQ/4, LLOQ/2), or without a value and reported as
# "n.d." / "n.q." (`conc` NA, `conc_flag`)
LLOX_IMPUTED <- !isFALSE(tr$params$impute_llox)
if (!HAS_CALIB) {   # Same columns, no rows
  conc_long <- tibble(.row_id = character(), feature_name = character(), sample_name = character(),
                      Class = character(), .ctrl_cat = character(), injection_order = integer(),
                      batch_id = character(), conc = numeric(), conc0 = numeric(), lod = numeric(),
                      lloq = numeric(), max_c_conc = numeric(), uloq = numeric(), has_proper_range = logical(),
                      src_calcurve = character(), conc_flag = character())
}
status_levels <- c("Valid", "> ULOQ, within curve", "> ULOQ, extrapolated", "< LLOQ", "< LOD", "Not detected", "No valid calibration",
                   "Removed (blank filter)", "Removed (QC RSD%)")
# Colour-blind safe (Okabe-Ito)
status_colors <- c("Valid" = "#009E73", "> ULOQ, within curve" = "#CFCB8F", "> ULOQ, extrapolated" = "#999933", "< LLOQ" = "#C9A400", "< LOD" = "#E69F00",
                   "Not detected" = "#D9D9D9", "No valid calibration" = "#D55E00",
                   "Removed (blank filter)" = "#CC79A7", "Removed (QC RSD%)" = "#0072B2")
conc_long <- conc_long |>
  mutate(status = case_when(
    !has_proper_range ~ "No valid calibration",
    is.na(conc0) ~ "Not detected",
    conc0 < lod ~ "< LOD",
    conc0 < lloq ~ "< LLOQ",
    # No ULOQ (quadratic curve): no such status. Above the ULOQ but within the curve when the curve
    # was not cut at the ULOQ (--enforce_linear_range), extrapolated above the top of the curve
    !is.na(uloq) & conc0 > pmax(uloq, max_c_conc, na.rm = TRUE) ~ "> ULOQ, extrapolated",
    !is.na(uloq) & conc0 > uloq ~ "> ULOQ, within curve",
    TRUE ~ "Valid"
  ))
# Targeted compounds removed before calibration: one status per sample too
removed <- tr[["removed features"]]
if (is.null(removed) || nrow(removed) == 0) {
  removed <- tibble(mat_id = character(), feature_id = character(), feature_name = character(),
                    targeted = logical(), reason = character(), qc_rsd = numeric())
}
removed_tgt <- removed[removed$mat_id == MAT & removed$targeted, ]
if (HAS_CALIB && nrow(removed_tgt) > 0) {
  samples_q <- distinct(conc_long, sample_name, Class, .ctrl_cat, injection_order, batch_id)
  conc_long <- bind_rows(conc_long, tidyr::crossing(
    tibble(.row_id = removed_tgt$feature_id, feature_name = removed_tgt$feature_name,
           status = ifelse(removed_tgt$reason == "QC RSD%", "Removed (QC RSD%)", "Removed (blank filter)")),
    samples_q
  ))
}
conc_long$status <- factor(conc_long$status, levels = status_levels)
study_long <- filter(conc_long, .ctrl_cat == "")

# Calibration result per targeted compound (TComp) and batch, for the outcome in the m/z map
calib_rows <- purrr::map_dfr(names(lst), function(b) {
  SumExp::row_df(lst[[b]]$concn) |> tibble::as_tibble(rownames = "feature_id") |>
    select(feature_id, to_export, has_proper_range) |> mutate(batch = b)
})

kpi <- function(value, label, warn = FALSE, href = NULL) {
  box <- sprintf('<div class="kpi%s"><div class="v">%s</div><div class="l">%s</div></div>',
                 if (warn) " warn" else "", value, label)
  if (is.null(href)) box else sprintf('<a class="kpi-link" href="%s" title="Go to the section">%s</a>', href, box)
}
# All rows in a scrolling box, no pages (as in the app); `search = FALSE`: no table-wide search
# box (the column filters remain). Tables with many rows draw only the visible rows (Scroller),
# so that the report stays fast. `scroll` is not used any more (kept for the callers).
dt <- function(df, ..., search = TRUE, scroll = TRUE) {
  big <- nrow(df) > 1000
  opts <- list(scrollX = TRUE, scrollY = "400px", scrollCollapse = TRUE,
               dom = if (search) "Bfrti" else "Brti", buttons = c("copy", "csv"))
  opts <- if (big) c(opts, list(deferRender = TRUE, scroller = TRUE)) else c(opts, list(paging = FALSE))
  # No row selection: clicking a row has no effect in the report
  DT::datatable(df, rownames = FALSE, filter = "top", selection = "none",
                extensions = c("Buttons", if (big) "Scroller"), options = opts, ...)
}
sig <- function(v) signif(v, 4)
FAILED_BG <- "#F8D0D0"   # Background of table rows with a failed IS or calibration
KEPT_BG <- "#FFE3B3"     # Background of calibration curves kept although not valid
# Shared sample table for the viewers; points refer to it by index (keeps the embedded data small)
s_tab <- smp |> transmute(n = sample_name, c = Class, g = group, k = category,
                          b = as.character(batch_id), i = injection_order)
# Averaged calibration points (option "average calibration replicates per batch"): not samples of
# the data file, added so that the viewers can show them (ID = name, e.g. "CalAvg_B1_0.5")
AVERAGE_CAL <- isTRUE(tr$params$average_cal_reps)
cal_avg <- if (HAS_CALIB) {
  bind_rows(lapply(lst, \(x) tibble::as_tibble(SumExp::col_df(x$calcurve), rownames = "sample_id"))) |>
    filter(!sample_name %in% smp$sample_name) |> distinct(sample_name, .keep_all = TRUE)
}
if (!is.null(cal_avg) && nrow(cal_avg) > 0) {
  s_tab <- bind_rows(s_tab, transmute(cal_avg, n = sample_name, c = paste("Average of", n_averaged %||% NA, "replicates"),
                                      g = "Calibrant", k = "CalCurve", b = as.character(batch_id), i = injection_order))
}
s_idx <- setNames(seq_len(nrow(s_tab)) - 1L, s_tab$n)
id2name <- setNames(smp$sample_name, smp$sample_id)
if (!is.null(cal_avg) && nrow(cal_avg) > 0) id2name <- c(id2name, setNames(cal_avg$sample_name, cal_avg$sample_id))
to_json <- function(x) jsonlite::toJSON(x, auto_unbox = TRUE, null = "null", na = "null", digits = NA,
                                        dataframe = "columns")
```

# 1 Overview

```{r}
#| results: asis
cmp_stat <- study_long |> group_by(feature_name) |>
  summarise(detected = mean(status %in% c("Valid", "> ULOQ, within curve", "> ULOQ, extrapolated", "< LLOQ")) >= 0.5,
            quantified = any(status %in% c("Valid", "> ULOQ, within curve", "> ULOQ, extrapolated")))
cat('<div class="kpis">',
    kpi(sum(smp$category == "Study sample"), "Study samples"),
    if (has_qc) kpi(sum(smp$category == "QC"), "QC samples"),
    kpi(sum(smp$category == "Blank"), "Blanks"),
    kpi(sum(smp$category == "CalCurve"), "Calibration samples"),
    kpi(length(batch_ids), "Batches"),
    # All targeted (Quant) compounds of the file; their calibration status is in table 4.2
    if (HAS_CALIB) kpi(sum(feat$type == "Targeted"), "Targeted compounds &rarr;", href = "#calib-limits") else
      kpi(sum(feat$type == "Targeted"), "Targeted compounds"),
    if (HAS_CALIB) kpi(sum(cmp_stat$detected), "Compounds > LOD in ≥ 50% of study samples"),
    if (HAS_CALIB) kpi(sum(cmp_stat$quantified), "Compounds quantified in ≥ 1 study sample"),
    kpi(sum(feat$type == "Non-targeted"), "Non-targeted features"),
    kpi(sum(tr[["is failed internal std."]]), "Failed internal standards &rarr;", warn = TRUE, href = "#failed-is"),
    kpi(sum(tr[["is outlier sample"]], na.rm = TRUE), "Outlier samples removed &rarr;", warn = TRUE, href = "#outlier-samples"),
    '</div>', sep = "")
```


Sections with *tabs* show alternative views of the same data. Study samples are summarised **over the
whole experiment** (by group); batches appear where they matter for quality control. Large sets of plots
(one per compound or internal standard) are shown as one interactive plot with a dropdown.

## 1.1 Processing summary

::: {.panel-tabset}

### Per batch

```{r}
norm_cd <- SumExp::col_df(tr[["normalized"]])
cpb <- tr[["calibration per batch"]]
if (is.null(cpb)) cpb <- tibble(mat_id = character(), batch_id = character(), calibration = character(), note = character())
cpb <- cpb[cpb$mat_id == BLK, ]
tibble(
  Batch = batch_label(batch_ids),
  `Blank samples` = vapply(batch_ids, \(b) sum(norm_cd$batch_id == b & norm_cd$.ctrl_cat == "Blank"), integer(1)),
  `Blank subtracted` = ifelse(batch_ids %in% tr[["batches without blank"]], "Average of all batches", "Batch"),
  Calibration = coalesce(cpb$calibration[match(batch_ids, cpb$batch_id)], "None"),
  Note = coalesce(as.character(cpb$note[match(batch_ids, cpb$batch_id)]), "")
) |> dt()
```

### Settings

```{r}
p <- tr$params
val <- function(x) if (is.null(x) || length(x) == 0 || all(is.na(x))) "–" else paste(x, collapse = ", ")
rsd_f <- tr[["qc rsd filter"]]
rsd_txt <- if (!isTRUE(p$rsd_filter)) "No" else if (isTRUE(rsd_f$skipped)) "Skipped (no QC replicates)" else
  paste0("Yes (", p$rsd_filter_scope, "; max. targeted ", val(rsd_f$max_targeted),
         "%, non-targeted ", val(rsd_f$max_nontargeted), "%)")
tibble(Setting = c("Normalization (this report)", "Best normalization (lowest median RSD%)",
                   "Per-batch processing", "Outlier removal", "Blank filtering", "Blank filtering factor",
                   "QC RSD% filter", "Weighting", "LOD/LLOQ method", "RSD% ≤ 20% for LLOQ",
                   "Log-scale calibration", "Keep all calibration curves", "Linear models only",
                   "Linear range (ULOQ): max. deviation of the top level; curves cut at the ULOQ",
                   "Minimum R² of the calibration curves", "Values below the LOD/LLOQ",
                   "Calibration replicates averaged per batch (global curve)", "Pre-normalization by the volumetric IS"),
       Value = c(val(method_label[MAT]), val(method_label[tr[["best normalization"]]]),
                 val(length(batch_ids) > 1),
                 if (!isTRUE(p$rm_outlier)) "No" else if (identical(p$rm_outlier_scope, "no_calib"))
                   "Yes (calibration samples always kept)" else "Yes (all injections)",
                 val(p$blank_filter),
                 val(p$blank_filter_factor), rsd_txt, val(p$weight), val(p$llox_method),
                 val(p$use_rsd20), val(p$log_calibration), val(isTRUE(p$keep_all_calcurves)), val(isTRUE(p$linear_only)),
                 paste0(if (isTRUE(p$log_calibration)) "SCALiR" else if (is.null(p$linear_range_tol)) "–" else paste0(p$linear_range_tol, "%"),
                        "; ", if (isTRUE(p$enforce_linear_range)) "cut" else "not cut"),
                 if (isTRUE(p$r2_filter)) sprintf("%.3f", p$min_r2) else "None",
                 if (isFALSE(p$impute_llox)) "Reported as n.d. / n.q. (no value)" else "Replaced (LLOQ/4, LLOQ/2)",
                 val(isTRUE(p$average_cal_reps)),
                 if (is.null(tr[["vIS prenormalization"]])) "No" else paste("Yes:", paste(tr[["vIS prenormalization"]], collapse = ", then ")))) |>
  knitr::kable()
```

# 3 Quality control and normalization

```{r}
is0 <- tr[["internal std. before qc"]]                     # All IS, all samples, raw values
is_failed <- tr[["is failed internal std."]]
is_out <- tr[["is outlier sample"]]
n_out <- tr[["number of outlier internal std. per sample"]]
is_tbl <- SumExp::row_df(is0) |>
  tibble::as_tibble(rownames = "feature_id") |>
  mutate(rsd = show$compute_rsd_per_feature(is0[["raw"]]),
         zeros = proc$count_zeros_per_feature(is0[["raw"]]),
         failed = unname(is_failed))
is_cols <- function(d) transmute(d, `Internal standard` = feature_name, `Avg RT [min]` = round(.rt, 2),
                                 `Avg m/z` = round(mz, 5), `RSD% (raw, all samples)` = round(rsd, 1),
                                 `Zero values` = zeros)
# After removing failed IS and outlier samples (used for the RSD% below)
is_clean <- is0[!is_failed, if (is.null(is_out)) TRUE else !is_out]
```

## 3.1 Internal standards

There are `r nrow(is0)` internal standards (IS) in the data, measured in `r ncol(is0)` samples.

```{r}
is_cols(is_tbl) |> mutate(Status = ifelse(is_tbl$failed, "Failed (removed)", "OK")) |> dt() |>
  DT::formatStyle("Status", target = "row", backgroundColor = DT::styleEqual("Failed (removed)", FAILED_BG))
```

## 3.2 Failed internal standards {#failed-is}

An IS fails when more than 10% of the samples have a zero value. Failed IS are removed before
normalization.

```{r}

is_long <- function(se, ii) {

}
```

## 3.3 Outlier samples {#outlier-samples}

A sample is an outlier when more than 20% of the IS deviate by more than 3 standard deviations from
the IS mean (log scale). Outlier samples are removed before normalization.

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (is.null(is_out)) {
  note("Outlier removal was not selected.")
} else if (!any(is_out)) {
  note("No outlier samples were found.")
} else {
  smp |> filter(sample_id %in% names(which(is_out))) |>
    transmute(Sample = sample_name, `Sample type` = sample_type, `Class (group)` = Class,
              Batch = batch_id, `Injection order` = injection_order,
              `Outlying IS` = paste(n_out[sample_id], "of", nrow(is0))) |>
    knitr::kable()
}
```

## 3.4 Raw RSD%

RSD% of the raw IS peak areas within groups of samples, after removing failed IS and outlier samples.
A group with a single sample has no RSD% (it needs at least two); the *Note* column says so.
Filter the table by grouping or group; the matrix tab shows all groups side by side.

```{r}
rsd_of <- function(cols) apply(is_clean[["raw"]][, cols, drop = FALSE], 1, show$rsd_perc)
cd_clean <- SumExp::col_df(is_clean)
grp_rsd <- function(grouping, key, keep = TRUE) {
  keys <- unique(key[keep])
  purrr::map_dfr(keys, function(k) {
    cols <- keep & key == k
    # A group with a single sample stays in the table, with the reason why it has no RSD%
    rsd <- if (sum(cols) < 2) NA_real_ else round(rsd_of(cols), 1)
    tibble(`Internal standard` = SumExp::row_df(is_clean)$feature_name, Grouping = grouping, Group = k,
           n = sum(cols), `RSD%` = rsd,
           Note = dplyr::case_when(
             sum(cols) < 2 ~ paste0("Too few samples (n = ", sum(cols), "): RSD% needs at least 2"),
             !is.finite(rsd) ~ "Not computable: all values 0 or missing",
             TRUE ~ ""
           ))
  })
}
is_rsd <- bind_rows(
  grp_rsd("Sample type", cd_clean$sample_type),
  grp_rsd("Class", cd_clean$Class, cd_clean$sample_type != "QC"),
  if (has_qc) grp_rsd("QC group", cd_clean$Class, cd_clean$sample_type == "QC")
)
```

## 3.7 Internal standards over the sequence

The internal standards (IS) of each sample in injection order, stacked: switch the colours between
sample group, batch and the contribution of each IS, and the values between raw and normalized. The
line is a LOESS trend of the total. Drag to zoom, double-click to reset; hover over a bar for details.
Failed IS and outlier samples are left out. An IS normalized by itself (Closest RT) is 1 in every
sample, so the normalized totals are flat for that method.

```{r}
#| results: asis
is_se <- tr[["normalized"]][util$is_internal_std(tr[["normalized"]]), ]
is_io <- SumExp::col_df(is_se)$injection_order
is_methods <- intersect(c("raw", "closest_norm", "loess_norm", "mvis_norm"), names(method_label))
isbar <- list(
  names = SumExp::row_df(is_se)$feature_name,
  is_colors = unname(show$hue_colors(SumExp::row_df(is_se)$feature_name)),   # As in the app
  batch_colors = as.list(show$hue_colors(paste("Batch", sort(unique(as.character(SumExp::col_df(is_se)$batch_id)))))),
  group_order = names(group_colors),
  s = unname(s_idx[SumExp::col_df(is_se)$sample_name]),
  methods = unname(method_label[is_methods]),
  v = lapply(setNames(is_methods, method_label[is_methods]), \(m) unname(sig(is_se[[m]]))),
  trend = lapply(setNames(is_methods, method_label[is_methods]), function(m) {
    tot <- colSums(is_se[[m]], na.rm = TRUE)
    fit <- tryCatch(stats::loess(tot ~ is_io, span = 0.3), error = \(e) NULL)
    if (is.null(fit)) return(NULL)
    o <- order(is_io)
    list(x = is_io[o], y = sig(stats::predict(fit)[o]))
  })
)
cat('<div class="viewer" id="isbar">',
    '<div class="controls"><label>Colour <select class="colour">',
    '<option value="group">Sample group</option><option value="batch">Batch</option>',
    '<option value="is">Internal standard</option></select></label>',
    '<label>Values <select class="values"></select></label></div>',
    '<div class="plot" style="height:520px;"></div></div>',
    '<script>window.ISBAR = ', to_json(isbar), ';</script>', sep = "")
```

```{r}
#| label: norm-eval-functions
norm_all <- tr[["normalized"]]
norm_cd <- tibble::as_tibble(SumExp::col_df(norm_all), rownames = "sample_id") |>
  left_join(select(smp, sample_id, group), by = "sample_id")
not_is <- !util$is_internal_std(norm_all)
norm_se <- norm_all[util$is_targeted_feature(norm_all), ]

# QC RSD% of the targeted compounds, raw vs normalized
plot_rsd <- function(m) {
  if (!has_qc_rep) return(note(NO_QC))
  if (nrow(norm_se) == 0) return(note("No targeted compounds in this dataset."))
  d <- tibble(Compound = SumExp::row_df(norm_se)$feature_name,
              raw = proc$qc_rsd_per_feature(norm_se, "raw"), norm = proc$qc_rsd_per_feature(norm_se, m)) |>
    filter(is.finite(raw), is.finite(norm))
  lim <- c(0, min(150, max(c(d$raw, d$norm))))
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(raw, norm, text = paste0(Compound, "<br>raw ", round(raw, 1), "% → ", round(norm, 1), "%"))) +
    geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, color = "grey60", linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_point(aes(color = norm < raw), size = 2, alpha = .8) +
    scale_color_manual(values = c(`TRUE` = "#009E73", `FALSE` = "#D55E00"), labels = c(`TRUE` = "Improved", `FALSE` = "Not improved"), name = NULL) +
    coord_cartesian(xlim = lim, ylim = lim) +
    labs(x = "QC RSD% raw", y = paste0("QC RSD% ", method_label[m]),
         title = sprintf("Median QC RSD%%: raw %.1f%% → %.1f%%; improved for %d of %d compounds",
                         median(d$raw), median(d$norm), sum(d$norm < d$raw), nrow(d)))
  plotly::ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text", height = 480)
}
# Relative log abundance (RLA) per sample along the injection order: the median deviation of each
# sample from the feature medians of the study samples and QCs; normalization should bring it
# close to 0 everywhere. Blanks and calibrants (no sample matrix) are not shown.
in_matrix <- norm_cd$group %in% c(study_classes, "QC")
plot_rla <- function(m) {
  if (!any(in_matrix)) return(note("No study samples or QCs: no relative log abundance."))
  rla <- function(mat) {
    lx <- log2(ifelse(mat > 0, mat, NA))[, in_matrix, drop = FALSE]   # Also with one sample
    apply(lx - apply(lx, 1, median, na.rm = TRUE), 2, median, na.rm = TRUE)
  }
  d <- bind_rows(lapply(c("raw", m), function(mm) {
    mutate(norm_cd[in_matrix, ], method = method_label[mm], rla = rla(norm_all[[mm]][not_is, ]))
  })) |>
    mutate(method = factor(method, levels = method_label[c("raw", m)]))
  p <- ggplot(d, aes(injection_order, rla, color = group, text = paste0(sample_name, " (batch ", batch_id, ")"))) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "grey60") +
    geom_point(size = 1.4, alpha = .8) +
    facet_wrap(~method, ncol = 1) +
    scale_color_manual(values = group_colors) +
    labs(x = "Injection order", y = "Median relative log2 abundance", color = NULL)
  plotly::ggplotly(p, tooltip = "text", height = 520)
}
# PCA of the study samples (and QCs), raw vs normalized, coloured by batch or by sample group
# The PCA of each matrix is computed once and reused (both colourings, and "raw" in every method)
pca_cache <- new.env()
plot_pca <- function(m, by = c("batch", "group")) {
  by <- match.arg(by)
  keep_s <- norm_cd$group != "Calibrant" & norm_cd$group != "Blank"
  d <- bind_rows(lapply(c("raw", m), function(mm) {
    if (!exists(mm, envir = pca_cache, inherits = FALSE)) assign(mm, pca_scores(mm, keep_s), envir = pca_cache)
    get(mm, envir = pca_cache)
  }))
  pca_draw(d, by)
}
# PC1 and PC2 of the study samples and QCs of one matrix (`NULL` if a PCA is not possible)
pca_scores <- function(mm, keep_s) {
  x <- norm_all[[mm]][not_is, keep_s, drop = FALSE]   # `drop = FALSE`: also with one sample
  x <- x[rowSums(is.na(x)) == 0 & apply(x, 1, sd) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
  if (nrow(x) < 2 || ncol(x) < 2) return(NULL)        # A PCA needs 2 samples and 2 features
  pc <- prcomp(t(log1p(x)), scale. = TRUE, rank. = 2)  # Only PC1 and PC2 are needed
  ve <- round(100 * pc$sdev^2 / sum(pc$sdev^2), 1)
  mutate(norm_cd[keep_s, ], PC1 = pc$x[, 1], PC2 = if (ncol(pc$x) > 1) pc$x[, 2] else 0,
         method = sprintf("%s (PC1 %s%%, PC2 %s%%)", method_label[mm], ve[1], ve[2]))
}
pca_draw <- function(d, by) {
  if (nrow(d) == 0) {
    return(note("No PCA: it needs at least 2 study samples or QCs and 2 features without missing values."))
  }
  if (by == "batch") {
    ggplot(d, aes(PC1, PC2, color = factor(batch_id), shape = group == "QC")) +
      geom_point(size = 2, alpha = .8) +
      facet_wrap(~method, scales = "free") +
      scale_shape_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = 16, `TRUE` = 17), labels = c(`FALSE` = "Study sample", `TRUE` = "QC"), name = NULL) +
      labs(color = "Batch")
  } else {
    ggplot(d, aes(PC1, PC2, color = group)) +
      geom_point(size = 2, alpha = .8) +
      facet_wrap(~method, scales = "free") +
      scale_color_manual(values = group_colors) +
      labs(color = "Sample group")
  }
}
rla_text <- paste(
  "Each point is one sample: its relative log abundance (RLA) [@delivera2012], the median, over all",
  "features, of log2(the feature's value in this sample / the feature's median in all study samples",
  "and QCs). 0 means a sample of typical overall",
  "intensity; a shift of the whole sample (dilution, injection volume, signal drift) moves it up or",
  "down. A good normalization brings all samples close to 0, in every batch."
)
rsd_text <- paste(
  "Each point is one targeted compound: its RSD% among the QC replicates before normalization (raw",
  "peak areas, x-axis) and after this normalization (y-axis). The RSD% is computed within each QC",
  "group with at least two samples; with several groups, their median is used. The values are before",
  "blank filtering and blank subtraction. Points below the dashed diagonal (green) became more precise",
  "with this normalization, points above it (red) less precise. The axes end at 150%."
)
pca_text <- paste(
  "Principal component analysis (PCA) of the study samples and QCs (no blanks or calibration samples),",
  "on all features except the internal standards: the targeted compounds, the non-targeted features",
  "and the volumetric IS, before blank filtering. Left: the raw peak areas; right: the features after",
  "this normalization (corrected with the internal standards, not the internal standards themselves).",
  "Each panel is its own PCA, of log(value + 1) with every feature scaled to unit variance; features",
  "with missing values or without variation are left out. The panel titles give the variance explained",
  "by PC1 and PC2."
)
pca_batch_text <- paste(
  "Coloured by batch (triangles: QCs). A batch effect shows as batches in separate clouds; a good",
  "normalization brings the batches together and the QCs close to each other."
)
pca_group_text <- paste(
  "Coloured by sample group. The differences between the study groups should remain (or become",
  "clearer) after normalization, while the QCs stay close together."
)
```

lowest RSD% (raw peak areas are not a method); all other compounds are the grey lines behind it.
Choose the compound in the dropdown or search; hover over a point for its value.

```{r}
#| results: asis
if (!show$has_enough_qc(norm_all)) note(show$not_enough_qc_msg) else if (nrow(norm_se) == 0) note(NO_TCOMP) else {
  labs_m <- SumExp::name_labs(norm_all)
  names(labs_m) <- gsub(" .*", "", names(labs_m))   # First word only, as in the app
  rsd_cmp <- show$extract_quant_qc(norm_all) |>
    show$calc_rsd_qstd(labs_m) |>
    show$mark_lowest_rsd_norm(labs_m) |>
    left_join(select(feat, feature_id, feature_name), by = "feature_id")
  qc_groups <- sort(unique(rsd_cmp$QC))   # Panels in the order of the app
  ids <- unique(rsd_cmp$feature_id[order(rsd_cmp$feature_name)])   # By compound name
  rsd_view <- list(
    # I(): arrays also for a single QC group
    methods = I(names(labs_m)), groups = I(qc_groups), sign_colors = as.list(show$norm_sign_colors),
    comps = lapply(ids, function(id) {
      d <- rsd_cmp[rsd_cmp$feature_id == id, ]
      list(name = d$feature_name[1],
           r = lapply(qc_groups, function(g) {
             i <- match(g, d$QC)
             if (is.na(i)) NULL else I(unname(round(unlist(d[i, unname(labs_m)]), 1)))
           }),
           s = I(unname(vapply(qc_groups, function(g) { i <- match(g, d$QC); if (is.na(i)) "" else as.character(d$sign[i]) }, ""))))
    })
  )
  n_rows <- ceiling(length(qc_groups) / min(length(qc_groups), 3))
  cat('<div class="viewer" id="rsdv">',
      '<div class="controls"><input type="search" class="search" placeholder="Search…" size="14"><button type="button" class="prev">&#9664;</button><select class="sel"></select>',
      '<button type="button" class="next">&#9654;</button></div>',
      '<div class="info"></div><div class="plot" style="height:', 60 + 280 * n_rows, 'px;"></div></div>',
      '<script>window.RSDVIEW = ', to_json(rsd_view), ';</script>', sep = "")
}
```

## 3.10 Removed features

Features removed by the blank filter and, when selected, by the QC RSD% filter (thresholds as
discussed by @broadhurst2018).

```{r}
if (is.null(removed) || nrow(filter(removed, mat_id == MAT)) == 0) {
  note("No features were removed for this normalization method.")
} else {
  removed |> filter(mat_id == MAT) |>
    left_join(select(feat, feature_id, label, ftype = type), by = "feature_id") |>
    # The volumetric IS has its own type
    transmute(Feature = coalesce(label, feature_name),
              Type = case_when(targeted ~ "Targeted", ftype %in% "Volumetric IS" ~ "Volumetric IS", TRUE ~ "Non-targeted"),
              `Removed by` = reason, `QC RSD%` = round(qc_rsd, 1)) |> dt(search = FALSE)
}
```

## 3.11 Blanks compared to samples

One targeted compound at a time in the (method) blanks, in red, next to the QCs, study samples and
calibrants, `r method_label[MAT]` values before blank filtering and blank subtraction. The dashed line is the threshold of the
blank filter: a feature is kept when its maximum or mean in the other samples (calibrants included) is
above `r tr$blank_filter_factor %||% 5` × its mean in the blanks (on blanks and QC samples in
metabolomics, see @broadhurst2018); internal standards are not filtered. Search, and switch between a bar per group (mean ± SD, samples as
points) and a bar per sample along the injection order. This report shows the targeted compounds only
(all features would make the report very large); the app (3.11) shows all features, also the
non-targeted ones and the internal standards.

```{r}
#| results: asis
norm_b <- tr[["normalized"]]
if (!any(util$ctrl_smpl_cat(norm_b) == "Blank")) {
  note("No blank samples in this dataset.")
} else if (!any(util$is_targeted_feature(norm_b))) {
  note(paste("No targeted (Quant) compounds in this dataset, so there is no interactive plot here: the",
             "report shows the targeted compounds only. The app (3.11) shows the blanks of all features."))
} else {
  rd_b <- SumExp::row_df(norm_b)
  type_b <- dplyr::case_when(
    rd_b$.std_type %in% "vIS" ~ "is",            # Volumetric IS with the internal standards
    util$is_internal_std(rd_b$.std_type) ~ "is",
    util$is_targeted_feature(rd_b$.std_type) ~ "targeted",
    TRUE ~ "nontargeted"
  )
  rem_b <- removed$feature_id[removed$mat_id == MAT & removed$reason == "Blank filter"]
  # The targeted compounds only (by name)
  ord_b <- which(type_b == "targeted")
  ord_b <- ord_b[order(feat$label[match(rownames(rd_b)[ord_b], feat$feature_id)])]
  blank_view <- list(
    f = lapply(ord_b, function(i) list(
      name = feat$label[match(rownames(rd_b)[i], feat$feature_id)], t = type_b[i],
      r = rownames(rd_b)[i] %in% rem_b, y = unname(sig(norm_b[[MAT]][i, ])))),
    s = unname(s_idx[SumExp::col_df(norm_b)$sample_name]),
    factor = tr$blank_filter_factor %||% 5, used = isTRUE(tr$params$blank_filter),
    y_lab = paste(method_label[MAT], if (MAT == "raw") "peak area" else "normalized peak area")
  )
  cat('<div class="viewer" id="blankv">',
      # (One feature type: the targeted compounds; the hidden selector keeps the viewer code as in the app)
      '<div class="controls"><select class="type" style="display:none"><option value="targeted">Targeted</option></select>',
      '<input type="search" class="search" placeholder="Search…" size="14"><button type="button" class="prev">&#9664;</button><select class="sel"></select>',
      '<button type="button" class="next">&#9654;</button>',
      '<select class="view"><option value="groups">Groups</option><option value="samples">Per sample</option></select>',
      '<label><input type="checkbox" class="removed"> Only removed by the blank filter</label>',
      '<label><input type="checkbox" class="cal"> Calibrants</label>',
      '<label><input type="checkbox" class="log"> Log scale</label></div>',
      '<div class="info"></div><div class="plot" style="height:480px;"></div></div>',
      '<script>window.BLANKVIEW = ', to_json(blank_view), ';</script>', sep = "")
}
```

# 5 Whole experiment

The study samples **as one experiment**: groups compared over all batches.

## 5.1 PCA

```{r}
blk_lst <- tr[["normalized - blank"]]
m <- do.call(cbind, lapply(blk_lst, \(se) se[[BLK]]))
cd <- bind_rows(lapply(blk_lst, \(se) tibble::as_tibble(SumExp::col_df(se), rownames = "sample_id")))
keep_s <- cd$.ctrl_cat %in% c("", "QC")
m <- m[, keep_s, drop = FALSE]; cd <- cd[keep_s, ]   # `drop = FALSE`: also with one sample
m <- m[rowSums(is.na(m)) == 0 & apply(m, 1, sd) > 0, , drop = FALSE]
# A PCA needs at least 2 samples and 2 features (without missing values, with variation)
PCA_MSG <- sprintf("No PCA: it needs at least 2 samples and 2 features without missing values; there are %d samples and %d features.", ncol(m), nrow(m))
pca_ok <- ncol(m) >= 2 && nrow(m) >= 2
if (pca_ok) {
  pca <- prcomp(t(log1p(m)), scale. = TRUE, rank. = 2)   # Only PC1 and PC2 are needed
  ve <- round(100 * pca$sdev^2 / sum(pca$sdev^2), 1)
  pc <- tibble(PC1 = pca$x[, 1], PC2 = if (ncol(pca$x) > 1) pca$x[, 2] else 0, cd) |>
    mutate(group = ifelse(.ctrl_cat == "QC", "QC", Class))
}
```

```{r}
  geom_point(size = 2, alpha = .8) +
```

# Appendix {.unnumbered}

Built with QuaNTA from `r basename(user_inputs$input_file)` (an MS-DIAL export [@tsugawa2015]);
normalization `r method_label[MAT]`; generated `r GENERATED_AT`. The layout of this report is inspired
by the quality control reports of MeTaQuaC [@kuhring2020].

```{r}
#| results: asis
# Hosting acknowledgement (SciLifeLab Serve's suggested wording), when generated on Serve
if (isTRUE(as.logical(params$on_serve))) {
  cat("Technical infrastructure for hosting the app 'QuaNTA' was provided by SciLifeLab Serve",
      "(https://serve.scilifelab.se; RRID:SCR_027820), a platform developed and supported by",
      "SciLifeLab Data Centre.\n\n")
}
```

**Software.** R [@rcore], Shiny [@shiny], Quarto [@quarto], ggplot2 [@ggplot2], plotly [@plotly], DT
[@dt]; the app runs in a Rocker container [@rocker2017].

**QuaNTA rules (no literature reference).** Each value is decided once, from its signal: `r if (LLOX_IMPUTED) "with a signal below the LOD signal it is replaced by LLOQ/4 (not detected), with a signal from the LOD signal to below the mean signal of the LLOQ level by LLOQ/2 (detected, not quantified)," else "with a signal below the LOD signal it is reported as n.d. (not detected), with a signal from the LOD signal to below the mean signal of the LLOQ level as n.q. (detected, not quantified), without a value (this processing did not replace them);"`
whatever its calculated concentration; with a signal at or above the mean signal of the LLOQ level
and a concentration below the LLOQ it is set to the LLOQ. Outlier samples: more than 20% of the internal standards
deviate by more than 3 standard deviations from their mean (log scale).

```{=html}
<script>
window.addEventListener('load', function () {
  // Tables in scrolling boxes inside tabs: align the column headers when a tab is shown
  document.addEventListener('shown.bs.tab', function () {
    if (window.jQuery && jQuery.fn.dataTable) jQuery.fn.dataTable.tables({ visible: true, api: true }).columns.adjust();
  });
  var S = window.QSAMPLES, COL = window.QCOLORS;
  // From 1000 on in scientific notation (as in the app), e.g. 1.234E+3; otherwise 4 significant digits
  var fmt = function (v) {
    if (v === null || v === undefined) return '–';
    return Math.abs(+v) >= 1000 ? (+v).toExponential(3).toUpperCase() : String(+(+v).toPrecision(4));
  };
  // Scientific notation (peak areas in 3.5 and 3.7, as in the app), e.g. 1.234E+6
  var sci = function (v) { return v === null || v === undefined ? '–' : (+v).toExponential(3).toUpperCase(); };
  var who = function (s) { return '<b>' + S.n[s] + '</b><br>' + S.c[s] + ' · batch ' + S.b[s] + ' · inj. ' + S.i[s]; };
  var font = { family: 'Lato, Segoe UI, sans-serif' };

  // A viewer: dropdown of items, previous / next buttons and redraw on any control change
  function viewer(id, items, label, draw) {
    var root = document.getElementById(id); if (!root) return;
    var sel = root.querySelector('.sel'), search = root.querySelector('.search'), labels = items.map(label);
    // Options matching the search text (case-insensitive); the current item stays selected if it matches
    function fill(q) {
      var cur = sel.value; sel.innerHTML = '';
      labels.forEach(function (t, i) {
        if (q && t.toLowerCase().indexOf(q) < 0) return;
        var o = document.createElement('option'); o.value = i; o.textContent = t; sel.appendChild(o);
      });
      if (Array.prototype.some.call(sel.options, function (o) { return o.value === cur; })) sel.value = cur;
    }
    fill('');
    search.addEventListener('input', function () {
      var before = sel.value; fill(search.value.trim().toLowerCase());
      if (sel.options.length && sel.value !== before) draw(root);
    });
    root.querySelectorAll('select, input:not(.search)').forEach(function (el) { el.addEventListener('change', function () { if (sel.options.length) draw(root); }); });
    root.querySelector('.prev').addEventListener('click', function () { if (sel.selectedIndex > 0) { sel.selectedIndex--; draw(root); } });
    root.querySelector('.next').addEventListener('click', function () { if (sel.selectedIndex < sel.options.length - 1) { sel.selectedIndex++; draw(root); } });
    draw(root);
  }

  // ---- Internal standards: box plot per group and scatter along the injection order ----
  var IV = window.ISVIEW;
  viewer('isv', IV.is, function (it) { return it.name + (it.failed ? '  (failed)' : ''); }, function (root) {
    var it = IV.is[+root.querySelector('.sel').value], isLog = root.querySelector('.log').checked, groups = {}, traces = [];
    IV.s.forEach(function (s, j) { (groups[S.g[s]] = groups[S.g[s]] || []).push(j); });
    Object.keys(groups).forEach(function (g) {
      var k = groups[g], y = k.map(function (j) { return it.y[j]; }), col = COL[g] || '#999';
      var txt = k.map(function (j) { return who(IV.s[j]) + '<br>peak area ' + sci(it.y[j]) + (IV.out[j] ? '<br><b>outlier sample</b>' : ''); });
      traces.push({ type: 'box', y: y, name: g, legendgroup: g, marker: { color: col }, boxpoints: false, xaxis: 'x', yaxis: 'y', showlegend: false, hoverinfo: 'y' });
      traces.push({ type: 'scatter', mode: 'markers', x: k.map(function (j) { return S.i[IV.s[j]]; }), y: y, name: g, legendgroup: g,
        marker: { color: col, size: 6, symbol: k.map(function (j) { return IV.out[j] ? 'x' : 'circle'; }) },
        text: txt, hovertemplate: '%{text}<extra></extra>', xaxis: 'x2', yaxis: 'y' });
    });
    root.querySelector('.info').innerHTML = it.failed ? '<span class="warn">Failed internal standard: removed before normalization.</span>' : '';
    Plotly.react(root.querySelector('.plot'), traces, {
      title: { text: it.name, x: 0.02 }, font: font, hovermode: 'closest', margin: { t: 50, r: 20, b: 60, l: 80 },
      // The groups panel keeps its x-axis when zooming; the shared y-axis zooms in both panels
      xaxis: { domain: [0, 0.27], tickangle: -30, fixedrange: true }, xaxis2: { domain: [0.32, 1], title: 'Injection order' },
      yaxis: { title: 'Peak area', type: isLog ? 'log' : 'linear', exponentformat: 'E', hoverformat: '.3e' }, legend: { orientation: 'v', x: 1.02, y: 1 }
    }, { responsive: true, displaylogo: false });
  });

  // ---- Internal standards over the sequence: stacked bars, coloured by group / batch / IS ----
  var B = window.ISBAR, bar = document.getElementById('isbar');
  if (B && bar) {
    var vals = bar.querySelector('.values'), colour = bar.querySelector('.colour');
    B.methods.forEach(function (m) { var o = document.createElement('option'); o.value = m; o.textContent = m; vals.appendChild(o); });
    var drawBars = function () {
      var m = vals.value, V = B.v[m], mode = colour.value, n = B.s.length, traces = [];
      var x = B.s.map(function (s) { return S.i[s]; });
      var tot = B.s.map(function (s, j) { return V.reduce(function (a, row) { return a + (row[j] || 0); }, 0); });
      var txt = function (j) { return who(B.s[j]) + '<br>total ' + sci(tot[j]); };
      if (mode === 'is') {
        V.forEach(function (row, i) {
          traces.push({ type: 'bar', x: x, y: row, name: B.names[i], marker: { color: B.is_colors[i] },
            text: row.map(function (v, j) { return txt(j) + '<br><b>' + B.names[i] + '</b> ' + sci(v); }),
            textposition: 'none', hovertemplate: '%{text}<extra></extra>' });
        });
      } else {
        var key = function (j) { var s = B.s[j]; return mode === 'batch' ? 'Batch ' + S.b[s] : S.g[s]; }, groups = {};
        for (var j = 0; j < n; j++) (groups[key(j)] = groups[key(j)] || []).push(j);
        // Groups in the order of the colour scheme (as in the app), batches sorted
        var order = mode === 'batch' ? Object.keys(B.batch_colors) : B.group_order;
        order.concat(Object.keys(groups).filter(function (g) { return order.indexOf(g) < 0; }).sort()).forEach(function (g) {
          if (!groups[g]) return;
          var idx = groups[g];
          traces.push({ type: 'bar', x: idx.map(function (j) { return x[j]; }), y: idx.map(function (j) { return tot[j]; }), name: g,
            marker: { color: (mode === 'batch' ? B.batch_colors[g] : COL[g]) || '#999' },
            text: idx.map(txt), textposition: 'none', hovertemplate: '%{text}<extra></extra>' });
        });
      }
      var tr = B.trend[m];
      if (tr) traces.push({ type: 'scatter', mode: 'lines', x: tr.x, y: tr.y, name: 'Trend (LOESS)', line: { color: '#2F5BEA', width: 3 }, hoverinfo: 'skip' });
      Plotly.react(bar.querySelector('.plot'), traces, {
        title: { text: 'Internal standards — ' + m, x: 0.02 }, barmode: 'stack', bargap: 0, hovermode: 'closest', font: font,
        xaxis: { title: 'Injection order' }, yaxis: { title: 'Summed IS peak area', exponentformat: 'E' },
        legend: { orientation: 'v', x: 1.02, y: 1 }, margin: { t: 50, r: 20, b: 60, l: 80 }
      }, { responsive: true, displaylogo: false });
    };
    vals.addEventListener('change', drawBars); colour.addEventListener('change', drawBars);
    drawBars();
  }

  // ---- Blanks compared to the sample groups (QC/QA): one feature, threshold of the blank filter ----
  var BV = window.BLANKVIEW, bv = document.getElementById('blankv');
  if (BV && bv) {
    var q = function (c) { return bv.querySelector(c); };
    var bsel = q('.sel'), bsearch = q('.search'), btype = q('.type'), brem = q('.removed');
    var mean = function (a) { return a.reduce(function (x, y) { return x + y; }, 0) / a.length; };
    var sd = function (a) { var m = mean(a); return a.length > 1 ? Math.sqrt(a.reduce(function (x, y) { return x + (y - m) * (y - m); }, 0) / (a.length - 1)) : 0; };
    // Features of the chosen type matching the search (and removed by the blank filter, if asked)
    var fillB = function () {
      var txt = bsearch.value.trim().toLowerCase(), t = btype.value, cur = bsel.value;
      bsel.innerHTML = '';
      BV.f.forEach(function (f, i) {
        if ((t !== 'all' && f.t !== t) || (brem.checked && !f.r) || (txt && f.name.toLowerCase().indexOf(txt) < 0)) return;
        var o = document.createElement('option'); o.value = i; o.textContent = f.name + (f.r ? '  (removed)' : ''); bsel.appendChild(o);
      });
      if (Array.prototype.some.call(bsel.options, function (o) { return o.value === cur; })) bsel.value = cur;
    };
    var drawB = function () {
      var plot = q('.plot'), info = q('.info');
      if (!bsel.options.length) { Plotly.react(plot, [], {}); info.innerHTML = '<span class="warn">No features of this kind.</span>'; return; }
      var f = BV.f[+bsel.value], withCal = q('.cal').checked, isLog = q('.log').checked, view = q('.view').value;
      var idx = BV.s.map(function (s, j) { return j; }).filter(function (j) { return f.y[j] !== null && (withCal || S.k[BV.s[j]] !== 'CalCurve'); });
      var groups = {}; idx.forEach(function (j) { var g = S.g[BV.s[j]]; (groups[g] = groups[g] || []).push(j); });
      // Blanks first, then QCs, the study groups (as the colour scheme) and the calibrants
      var order = ['Blank', 'QC'].concat(Object.keys(COL).filter(function (g) { return g !== 'Blank' && g !== 'QC' && g !== 'Calibrant'; }), ['Calibrant'])
        .filter(function (g) { return groups[g]; });
      var blanks = (groups['Blank'] || []).map(function (j) { return f.y[j]; }), thr = blanks.length ? BV.factor * mean(blanks) : null;
      var txt = function (j) { return who(BV.s[j]) + '<br>' + fmt(f.y[j]); }, traces = [], xaxis;
      if (view === 'groups') {
        order.forEach(function (g, i) {
          var k = groups[g], y = k.map(function (j) { return f.y[j]; });
          traces.push({ type: 'bar', x: [i + 1], y: [mean(y)], name: g, legendgroup: g, width: 0.7,
            error_y: { type: 'data', array: [sd(y)], color: '#4d4d4d' },
            marker: { color: COL[g] || '#999', opacity: 0.55, line: { color: COL[g] || '#999', width: 1.5 } },
            hovertemplate: '<b>' + g + '</b><br>mean ' + fmt(mean(y)) + ' (n = ' + k.length + ')<extra></extra>' });
          traces.push({ type: 'scatter', mode: 'markers', name: g, legendgroup: g, showlegend: false,
            x: k.map(function (j) { return i + 1 + (((j * 7919) % 100) / 100 - 0.5) * 0.5; }), y: y,
            marker: { color: COL[g] || '#999', size: 6, opacity: 0.8, line: { color: '#fff', width: 0.5 } },
            text: k.map(txt), hovertemplate: '%{text}<extra></extra>' });
        });
        xaxis = { tickvals: order.map(function (g, i) { return i + 1; }), ticktext: order, range: [0.4, order.length + 0.6], zeroline: false };
      } else {
        order.forEach(function (g) {
          var k = groups[g];
          traces.push({ type: 'bar', x: k.map(function (j) { return S.i[BV.s[j]]; }), y: k.map(function (j) { return f.y[j]; }), name: g, width: 0.9,
            marker: { color: COL[g] || '#999' }, text: k.map(txt), textposition: 'none', hovertemplate: '%{text}<extra></extra>' });
        });
        xaxis = { title: 'Injection order' };
      }
      // Threshold of the blank filter as a dashed line (a trace, so that it follows the log scale)
      if (thr !== null) {
        var xs = view === 'groups' ? [0.4, order.length + 0.6] : [Math.min.apply(null, idx.map(function (j) { return S.i[BV.s[j]]; })) - 1,
          Math.max.apply(null, idx.map(function (j) { return S.i[BV.s[j]]; })) + 1];
        traces.push({ type: 'scatter', mode: 'lines', x: xs, y: [thr, thr], name: 'Blank filter threshold (' + BV.factor + ' × blank mean)',
          line: { color: '#c23636', dash: 'dash', width: 2 }, hovertemplate: 'threshold ' + fmt(thr) + '<extra></extra>' });
      }
      info.innerHTML = !BV.used ? 'Blank filter not used in this processing.' :
        (f.r ? '<span class="warn">Removed by the blank filter.</span>' : '<span style="color:#2E9E5B;font-weight:600">Kept by the blank filter.</span>');
      Plotly.react(plot, traces, {
        title: { text: f.name, x: 0.02 }, barmode: 'overlay', bargap: view === 'samples' ? 0 : 0.2, hovermode: 'closest', font: font,
        xaxis: xaxis, yaxis: { title: BV.y_lab, type: isLog ? 'log' : 'linear', exponentformat: 'E' },
        legend: { orientation: 'v', x: 1.02, y: 1 }, margin: { t: 50, r: 20, b: 60, l: 80 }
      }, { responsive: true, displaylogo: false });
    };
    [btype, brem].forEach(function (el) { el.addEventListener('change', function () { fillB(); drawB(); }); });
    bsearch.addEventListener('input', function () { fillB(); drawB(); });
    ['.sel', '.view', '.cal', '.log'].forEach(function (c) { q(c).addEventListener('change', drawB); });
    q('.prev').addEventListener('click', function () { if (bsel.selectedIndex > 0) { bsel.selectedIndex--; drawB(); } });
    q('.next').addEventListener('click', function () { if (bsel.selectedIndex < bsel.options.length - 1) { bsel.selectedIndex++; drawB(); } });
    fillB(); drawB();
  }

  // ---- Comparison of normalization methods (3.8): one compound's QC RSD% per method, a panel per
  //      QC group, in the colour of its lowest method; all other compounds as grey lines behind ----
  var R = window.RSDVIEW;
  if (R && document.getElementById('rsdv')) {
    var nG = R.groups.length, nC = Math.min(nG, 3), nR = Math.ceil(nG / nC);
    var rsdOf = function (v) { return v === null ? 0 : v; };   // NA: all values 0 (as in the app)
    // All compounds of each QC group as one trace, the compounds separated by gaps
    var bgr = R.groups.map(function (g, gi) {
      var x = [], y = [];
      R.comps.forEach(function (c) {
        var r = c.r[gi]; if (!r) return;
        R.methods.forEach(function (m, mi) { x.push(m); y.push(rsdOf(r[mi])); });
        x.push(null); y.push(null);
      });
      return { x: x, y: y };
    });
    viewer('rsdv', R.comps, function (c) { return c.name; }, function (root) {
      var c = R.comps[+root.querySelector('.sel').value], traces = [], notes = [];
      var layout = { title: { text: c.name, x: 0.02 }, font: font, hovermode: 'closest', showlegend: false,
                     margin: { t: 60, r: 20, b: 40, l: 70 }, annotations: [] };
      R.groups.forEach(function (g, gi) {
        var ax = gi === 0 ? '' : String(gi + 1), col = gi % nC, row = Math.floor(gi / nC);
        var xd = [col / nC + 0.025, (col + 1) / nC - 0.025], yd = [1 - (row + 1) / nR + 0.1, 1 - row / nR - 0.05];
        layout['xaxis' + ax] = { domain: xd, anchor: 'y' + ax, type: 'category', categoryorder: 'array', categoryarray: R.methods };
        layout['yaxis' + ax] = { domain: yd, anchor: 'x' + ax, title: col === 0 ? 'RSD%' : '', rangemode: 'tozero' };
        layout.annotations.push({ text: '<b>' + g + '</b>', x: (xd[0] + xd[1]) / 2, y: yd[1], xref: 'paper', yref: 'paper',
                                  xanchor: 'center', yanchor: 'bottom', showarrow: false });
        traces.push({ x: bgr[gi].x, y: bgr[gi].y, mode: 'lines', type: 'scatter', connectgaps: false, hoverinfo: 'skip',
                      line: { color: 'rgba(110,110,110,0.18)', width: 1 }, xaxis: 'x' + ax, yaxis: 'y' + ax });
        var r = c.r[gi]; if (!r) return;
        var colr = R.sign_colors[c.s[gi]] || '#333';
        traces.push({ x: R.methods, y: r.map(rsdOf), mode: 'lines+markers', type: 'scatter', xaxis: 'x' + ax, yaxis: 'y' + ax,
                      line: { color: colr, width: 3 }, marker: { color: colr, size: 9 },
                      text: r.map(function (v, mi) { return '<b>' + c.name + '</b> (' + g + ')<br>' + R.methods[mi] + ': ' + (v === null ? 'NA (all 0s)' : (+v).toFixed(1) + '%'); }),
                      hovertemplate: '%{text}<extra></extra>' });
        notes.push('<span class="chip" style="color:' + colr + ';font-weight:600">' + g + ': lowest RSD% ' + c.s[gi].replace('↓ ', '') + '</span>');
      });
      root.querySelector('.info').innerHTML = notes.join(' ');
      Plotly.react(root.querySelector('.plot'), traces, layout, { responsive: true, displaylogo: false });
    });
  }

  // ---- QC samples in acquisition order (4.7): one compound, a line per QC group; measured values
  //      filled, values replaced by the LOD/LLOQ rules open; values without a value are counted ----
  var Q = window.QCVIEW;
  if (Q && document.getElementById('qcv')) {
    viewer('qcv', Q.comps, function (c) { return c.name; }, function (root) {
      var c = Q.comps[+root.querySelector('.sel').value], isLog = root.querySelector('.log').checked, traces = [], groups = {}, nf = {};
      c.s.forEach(function (s, j) {
        if (c.y[j] === null) { if (c.f[j]) nf[c.f[j]] = (nf[c.f[j]] || 0) + 1; return; }
        (groups[S.c[s]] = groups[S.c[s]] || []).push(j);
      });
      Object.keys(Q.group_colors).forEach(function (g) {
        var k = groups[g]; if (!k) return;
        k.sort(function (a, b) { return S.i[c.s[a]] - S.i[c.s[b]]; });
        var colr = Q.group_colors[g];
        traces.push({ type: 'scatter', mode: 'lines+markers', name: g, x: k.map(function (j) { return S.i[c.s[j]]; }),
          y: k.map(function (j) { return c.y[j]; }), line: { color: colr, width: 1 },
          marker: { size: 8, color: k.map(function (j) { return Q.kinds[c.k[j]] === 'Measured' ? colr : '#fff'; }), line: { color: colr, width: 1.5 } },
          text: k.map(function (j) { return who(c.s[j]) + '<br>conc. ' + fmt(c.y[j]) + ' ' + Q.unit + ' (' + Q.kinds[c.k[j]] + ')'; }),
          hovertemplate: '%{text}<extra></extra>' });
      });
      var nfTxt = Object.keys(nf).map(function (f) { return f + ' ' + nf[f]; }).join(', ');
      root.querySelector('.info').innerHTML = nfTxt ? 'Not shown (no value): ' + nfTxt : '';
      Plotly.react(root.querySelector('.plot'), traces, {
        title: { text: c.name, x: 0.02 }, hovermode: 'closest', font: font,
        xaxis: { title: 'Injection order' }, yaxis: { title: 'Concentration [' + Q.unit + ']', type: isLog ? 'log' : 'linear', exponentformat: 'E' },
        legend: { orientation: 'v', x: 1.02, y: 1, title: { text: 'QC group' } }, margin: { t: 50, r: 20, b: 60, l: 80 }
      }, { responsive: true, displaylogo: false });
    });
  }

  // ---- Concentrations per compound: a box per class, points coloured by measured / replaced ----
  var C = window.CONCVIEW;
  if (C && document.getElementById('concv')) {
    viewer('concv', C.comps, function (c) { return c.name; }, function (root) {
      var c = C.comps[+root.querySelector('.sel').value], isLog = root.querySelector('.log').checked;
      var classes = Object.keys(C.class_colors).filter(function (cl) { return c.s.some(function (s) { return S.c[s] === cl; }); });
      var pos = {}; classes.forEach(function (cl, i) { pos[cl] = i + 1; });
      var traces = classes.map(function (cl) {
        var y = c.y.filter(function (v, j) { return S.c[c.s[j]] === cl; });
        return { type: 'box', x: y.map(function () { return pos[cl]; }), y: y, name: cl, boxpoints: false, width: 0.6,
          fillcolor: C.class_colors[cl], opacity: 0.55, line: { color: '#4d4d4d', width: 1 }, hoverinfo: 'skip', showlegend: false };
      });
      C.kinds.forEach(function (kd, ki) {
        var k = c.k.map(function (v, j) { return v === ki ? j : -1; }).filter(function (j) { return j >= 0; });
        if (!k.length) return;
        traces.push({ type: 'scatter', mode: 'markers', name: kd,
          x: k.map(function (j) { return pos[S.c[c.s[j]]] + (((j * 7919) % 100) / 100 - 0.5) * 0.44; }),
          y: k.map(function (j) { return c.y[j]; }),
          marker: { color: C.kind_colors[ki], size: 7, opacity: 0.85, line: { color: '#fff', width: 0.5 } },
          text: k.map(function (j) { return who(c.s[j]) + '<br>conc. ' + fmt(c.y[j]) + ' ' + C.unit + ' (' + kd + ')'; }),
          hovertemplate: '%{text}<extra></extra>' });
      });
      Plotly.react(root.querySelector('.plot'), traces, {
        title: { text: c.name, x: 0.02 }, hovermode: 'closest', font: font,
        xaxis: { tickvals: classes.map(function (cl) { return pos[cl]; }), ticktext: classes, tickangle: -45,
                 range: [0.4, classes.length + 0.6], zeroline: false },
        yaxis: { title: 'Concentration [' + C.unit + ']', type: isLog ? 'log' : 'linear', exponentformat: 'E' },
        legend: { orientation: 'v', x: 1.02, y: 1, title: { text: 'Value' } }, margin: { t: 50, r: 20, b: 90, l: 80 }
      }, { responsive: true, displaylogo: false });
    });
  }

  // ---- Calibration curves: one compound, one curve (global or a batch) ----
  var D = window.CALVIEW, cv = document.getElementById('cv');
  if (!D || !cv) return;                       // No calibration in this report
  var vsel = cv.querySelector('.view');
  D.views.forEach(function (v) { var o = document.createElement('option'); o.value = v; o.textContent = v; vsel.appendChild(o); });
  vsel.value = D.views.length > 1 ? D.views[1] : D.views[0];
  viewer('cv', D.comps, function (c) {
    return c.name + (c.note ? '  (' + (c.note.indexOf('Removed') === 0 ? 'removed' : 'no valid curve') + ')' : '');
  }, function (root) {
    var c = D.comps[+root.querySelector('.sel').value], vn = root.querySelector('.view').value, v = c.v[vn];
    var isLog = root.querySelector('.log').checked, traces = [], shapes = [], notes = [], info = root.querySelector('.info');
    if (c.note) notes.push('<span class="warn">' + c.note + '</span>');
    if (!v) { Plotly.react(root.querySelector('.plot'), [], {}); info.innerHTML = notes.join(' '); return; }
    // Why the curve is not valid, kept although not valid, or replaced by the global one
    if (v.why && c.note.indexOf('Removed') !== 0) notes.push('<span class="' + (v.kept ? 'kept' : 'warn') + '">' + vn + ': ' + v.why + '.</span>');
    // No quantifiable sample: the full calibration range is shown
    if (v.nq) notes.push('<span class="kept">' + v.nq + '.</span>');
    if (v.model) notes.push('<span class="chip">Model: ' + v.model + '</span><span class="chip">R² ' + (v.r2 === null || v.r2 === undefined ? '–' : (+v.r2).toFixed(3)) + '</span>' +
      '<span class="chip">LOD ' + fmt(v.lod) + '</span><span class="chip">LLOQ ' + fmt(v.lloq) + '</span>' +
      '<span class="chip">ULOQ ' + (v.uloq === null || v.uloq === undefined ? '–' : fmt(v.uloq) + ' ' + D.unit) + '</span><span class="chip">Highest level ' + fmt(v.top) + ' ' + D.unit + '</span><span class="chip">Curve: ' + v.src + '</span>');
    info.innerHTML = notes.join(' ');
    // A curve that is not valid (e.g. R² below the minimum) is dashed
    if (v.curve) traces.push({ x: v.curve.x, y: v.curve.y, mode: 'lines', hoverinfo: 'skip',
      name: v.src === 'None' ? 'Calibration curve (not valid)' : 'Calibration curve',
      line: { color: v.src === 'None' ? '#c23636' : 'cadetblue', width: 2.5, dash: v.src === 'None' ? 'dash' : 'solid' } });
    // Calibration points: the zero calibrant (Cal0) in blue, the others used / not used for the curve
    [['cal0', 'Cal0 (zero calibrant)', 'diamond', '#1A0DF2'], [1, 'Calibration points (used)', 'circle', '#333'],
     [0, 'Calibration points (not used)', 'circle-open', '#888']].forEach(function (g) {
      var k = v.cal.u.map(function (u, j) {
        var isCal0 = v.cal.x[j] === 0;
        return (g[0] === 'cal0' ? isCal0 : (!isCal0 && u === g[0])) ? j : -1;
      }).filter(function (j) { return j >= 0; });
      if (!k.length) return;
      traces.push({ x: k.map(function (j) { return v.cal.x[j]; }), y: k.map(function (j) { return v.cal.y[j]; }),
        mode: 'markers', type: 'scatter', name: g[1], marker: { symbol: g[2], color: g[3], size: g[0] === 'cal0' ? 10 : 8 },
        text: k.map(function (j) { return who(v.cal.s[j]) + '<br>nominal ' + fmt(v.cal.x[j]) + ' ' + D.unit + ' · signal ' + fmt(v.cal.y[j]); }),
        hovertemplate: '%{text}<extra></extra>' });
    });
    if (v.smp) {
      var groups = {};
      v.smp.s.forEach(function (s, j) { (groups[S.g[s]] = groups[S.g[s]] || []).push(j); });
      Object.keys(groups).forEach(function (g) {
        var k = groups[g];
        traces.push({ x: k.map(function (j) { return v.smp.x[j]; }), y: k.map(function (j) { return v.smp.y[j]; }), mode: 'markers', type: 'scatter', name: g,
          marker: { color: COL[g] || '#999', size: 7, opacity: .85, line: { width: .5, color: '#fff' } },
          text: k.map(function (j) {
            var hasU = v.uloq !== null && v.uloq !== undefined;
            var x = v.smp.x[j], st = x < v.lod ? ' (< LOD)' : (x < v.lloq ? ' (< LLOQ)' :
              (hasU && x > Math.max(v.uloq, v.top) ? ' (> ULOQ, extrapolated)' : (hasU && x > v.uloq ? ' (> ULOQ, within curve)' : '')));
            return who(v.smp.s[j]) + '<br>conc. ' + fmt(x) + ' ' + D.unit + st + ' · signal ' + fmt(v.smp.y[j]);
          }),
          hovertemplate: '%{text}<extra></extra>' });
      });
    }
    // Shapes are placed by the concentration also on log axes (plotly.js 2.11: log10 values are
    // misplaced and stretch the axis)
    var lx = function (x) { return x; };
    if (v.lloq) {
      var x0 = isLog ? Math.min.apply(null, v.cal.x.filter(function (x) { return x > 0; }).concat([v.lod || v.lloq])) / 3 : 0;
      shapes.push({ type: 'rect', xref: 'x', yref: 'paper', x0: x0, x1: lx(v.lloq), y0: 0, y1: 1, fillcolor: 'rgba(80,80,80,.12)', line: { width: 0 } });
      if (v.lod) shapes.push({ type: 'rect', xref: 'x', yref: 'paper', x0: x0, x1: lx(v.lod), y0: 0, y1: 1, fillcolor: 'rgba(80,80,80,.18)', line: { width: 0 } });
    }
    // Above the ULOQ (the top of the linear range): shaded in olive up to the highest value shown
    if (v.uloq !== null && v.uloq !== undefined) {
      var xmax = Math.max.apply(null, v.cal.x.concat(v.smp ? v.smp.x : [], v.curve ? v.curve.x : []).filter(function (x) { return x !== null; }));
      if (xmax > v.uloq) shapes.push({ type: 'rect', xref: 'x', yref: 'paper', x0: lx(v.uloq), x1: lx(xmax), y0: 0, y1: 1, fillcolor: 'rgba(153,153,51,.15)', line: { width: 0 } });
      shapes.push({ type: 'line', xref: 'x', yref: 'paper', x0: lx(v.uloq), x1: lx(v.uloq), y0: 0, y1: 1, line: { color: '#999933', width: 1.5, dash: 'dash' } });
    }
    Plotly.react(root.querySelector('.plot'), traces, {
      title: { text: c.name + ' — ' + vn, x: 0.02 }, shapes: shapes, hovermode: 'closest', font: font,
      xaxis: { title: 'Concentration [' + D.unit + ']', type: isLog ? 'log' : 'linear', zeroline: false },
      yaxis: { title: D.y_lab, type: isLog ? 'log' : 'linear', zeroline: false, exponentformat: 'E' },
      legend: { orientation: 'v', x: 1.02, y: 1 }, margin: { t: 50, r: 20, b: 60, l: 80 }
    }, { responsive: true, displaylogo: false });
  });
});
</script>
```
